record.summary: Dr. Farhan Siddiqui, owner of a mid-sized dental clinic, received a one‑star review on a maps platform six weeks ago from a user calling themselves “Rahul K.”. The review alleged an unnecessary root canal, use of unsterilized tools and called the doctor a fraud. The clinic has no record of any patient named Rahul K. receiving a root canal, though a patient named Rahul Khanna had a filling six months ago and a billing dispute. Within two weeks of the review the clinic’s rating fell from 4.7 to 4.1. Over the next four weeks new‑patient bookings dropped sharply and three patients cancelled appointments, citing the review. Dr. Siddiqui has screenshots of the review, rating‑history data, booking‑system logs, cancellation messages, sterilisation logs, an inspection certificate and patient records. He sent a takedown request to the platform but received no response. He wants to know if he can sue for defamation, compel the platform to reveal the reviewer’s identity, have the review removed and recover lost income.
record.goal: Seek legal options for defamation, identity disclosure, removal of the review and compensation for alleged loss of income.
questions: What is the exact date and time shown on the screenshot when the review was posted?
Which maps platform hosted the review, and on what date and by what method did you send the takedown request?
Do you have an estimate of the monetary loss you attribute to the review (e.g., fees from cancelled appointments)?
In which city or state is the clinic located for jurisdictional purposes?
What specific remedy are you seeking – monetary damages, a court order to disclose the reviewer’s identity, removal of the review, or a combination of these?
evidence: Screenshots of the one‑star review with its timestamp.
Platform dashboard showing rating history drop from 4.7 to 4.1.
Booking‑system export indicating a decline in new appointments over four weeks compared with the previous four weeks.
Three cancellation messages from patients that mention the review.
Clinic sterilisation logs and an inspection certificate from three months ago showing compliance.
Patient records confirming a filling procedure for Rahul Khanna six months ago and the billing dispute.
